thread:
maria: FYI found a batch (~1.5k) of DB snapshot objects in prod without any SSE headers. Bucket: redwood-db-snapshots, prefix snapshots/2026-03-22/. This looks like plain uploads, no SSE metadata.
security-bot: [alert] object-store:missing-sse for snapshots/2026-03-22/ detected. severity=high. Alert ID: AS-2026-314. https://alerts.redwood.internal/AS-2026-314
aj: Can you paste one of the object's HEAD output? need to know if encryption metadata was stripped or never set.
maria: sample HEAD:
```
Content-Length: 209715200
x-amz-meta-origin: backup-service
x-amz-server-side-encryption: <not-present>
```
aj: interesting. I just queried CloudTrail for PutObject to that prefix 2026-03-22T02:00:00Z..2026-03-22T03:00:00Z. Results: 1,482 PutObject by principal arn:aws:iam::0123456789:role/svc-uploader-role. No kms:GrantTokens in call context.
luca: we shipped a small uploader metadata refactor last night (PR #4981). It moves SSE injection later in the pipeline; could be a race condition with multi-part uploads.
maria: is this a case of objects uploaded without SSE at all (i.e., cleartext)? or were they encrypted client-side then SSE header removed by proxy?
aj: CloudTrail S3 responses show 200 OK on PutObject with no error; no subsequent CopyObject calls. So objects are likely unencrypted server-side.
sam-oncall: immediate action: prevent further unencrypted uploads. Options: 1) temporarily revoke PutObject for svc-uploader-role on that bucket; 2) apply a bucket policy requiring s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption == aws:kms. Which do we prefer?
luca: bucket policy is safer and immediate, but be careful with other processes that legitimately write without SSE (rare). Quick policy snippet:
```
"Condition": {
  "StringNotEquals": { "s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption": "aws:kms" }
}
```
sam-oncall: I'll apply a deny policy requiring SSE for the snapshots prefix and monitor for errors.
aj: also collecting the full object key list and owners now. I'll export to CSV to attach to the incident.
maria: any KMS grant TTL changes recently? We tweaked ephemeral grant TTL for uploader to 2m earlier this month.
luca: I don't see KMS errors in CloudWatch; this looks like metadata injection never happened. Reproducer locally: multipart uploader writes parts then completes; post-complete metadata hook failed in the refactor.
erin: compliance needs timeline + proof for customers. If data was in cleartext on S3 even briefly, that's a compliance incident.
maria: severity P1 until we confirm all affected keys and whether any downstream replication copied them to other regions.
aj: replication check: none of the affected keys show replication status set; cross-region replication is off for that prefix. Good.
luca: remediation plan:
  - stop further unencrypted writes (sam-oncall)
  - run aws s3 cp --metadata-directive REPLACE to re-upload objects with --sse aws:kms and kms-key-id alias/redwood-cmk for a small sample (luca)
  - validate checksums after copy and record ETag differences (aj)
  - create list of affected snapshots and their tenant associations for CS/Legal (maria + erin)
  - roll back the metadata refactor or patch uploader to inject SSE earlier and add unit/integration tests (luca)

aj: note on the re-encrypt step: S3 copy will re-encrypt but will change ETag for non-multipart objects. For multipart we need to use multipart copy and validate with a recomputed SHA256 if required.
sam-oncall: applied deny bucket policy to snapshots/2026-03-22/* at 03:40Z. Will keep it until patch is rolled out.
maria: erin, can you confirm reporting requirements? Which customers require notification?
erin: I'll triage per contract. If any customers have active restores or contractual obligations around encryption, they get notified. Collecting affected tenant IDs.
aj: uploaded CSV (object-key, size, uploader-principal, put-timestamp) to the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood.internal/INC-2026-190
luca: I pushed a hotfix branch that restores explicit SSE injection earlier in the pipeline. Deploying canary to staging now.
maria: follow-ups post-incident:
  - add a bucket-level reject policy for missing SSE on all snapshot buckets
  - add a telemetry alert for PutObject without x-amz-server-side-encryption header (CloudTrail + Athena query)
  - revert risky TTL experiment for KMS grants until we prove uploader robustness
  - update runbook for unencrypted-upload incidents with clear steps and owners

security-bot: Incident created INC-2026-190, severity=P1, responders=@maria @aj @luca @sam-oncall @erin
sam-oncall: I've notified CS about 3 customers who had pending restores. CS will reach out.
maria: thanks. once aj's CSV is validated we'll start bulk re-encrypt for confirmed items. Keep this thread for coordination and paste any blocking errors here.
aj: starting checksum validation on sample copy. will post results in incident doc.
luca: canary passed in staging, patch will go to prod in 15m. I'll monitor uploader logs for metadata injection failures.
maria: good work team. We'll schedule a postmortem and include lessons learned in the encryptops runbook. :thumbsup:
